column26:
I’m running for RTD Board District K because RTD should work better for the people who actually rely on it. My top priorities are pretty simple: the bus needs to come on time, stations and vehicles need to feel safe, and riders need to be able to trust that RTD will get them where they’re going.

I also want RTD to think more seriously about how transit connects to housing, jobs, schools, and everyday life. RTD owns a lot of land near stations and park-n-rides, and we should be using those assets responsibly to support affordable, transit-oriented housing while staying focused on RTD’s core job: moving people.

I grew up in Commerce City, and I know how much better transit could help families across Adams County. I’m running because I think we need practical, accountable leadership that’s focused on the basics: reliable service, safer stations, better communication, and a system that gives people more freedom to get where they need to go.

I was born and raised in Colorado to Vietnamese refugees from the Vietnam War. I'm the the first in my family to go to college, graduating with a dual degree in Political Science and Communications from the University of Colorado Boulder. I recently completed my Master's of Public Administration (MPA) from the University of Colorado Denver in 2025.
Professionally, I served as an AmeriCorps Service Member for the Boulder “I Have a Dream” Foundation and as a community organizer for the Jared Polis for Governor campaign in 2018. I served as the Executive Assistant to Colorado’s Lieutenant Governor, Dianne Primavera, for over five years. As your State Representative, my goal is to ensure that Colorado’s most vulnerable communities are protected. Nationally, we are facing an erosion of Medicaid and education funding. This wrongfully targets Colorado’s most vulnerable. My belief is that government is by the people and for the people.

column26: My top priorities this term are the fights that matter most to working families in Southwest Denver and across Colorado. I am leading the effort to pass the Worker Protection Act, the biggest labor bill in Colorado history, which would end Colorado's status as a modified right-to-work state and give workers the power to organize and fight for living wages. I am championing HB 1210 to ban surveillance pricing, which stops corporations from using algorithms to spy on us and charge us more based on what we can afford. I am fighting to end wage garnishment for medical debt, so that a health crisis doesn't become a permanent financial one, and I am leading the push to create a state civil cause of action so that Coloradans can hold ICE agents accountable when they violate people's constitutional rights. Housing affordability has defined my legislative career. I passed Colorado's Just Cause for Eviction Law in 2024, one of the most progressive renter protections in the country, and I passed legislation banning the rent-setting algorithms that corporate landlords use to artificially inflate rents. I have taken on big pharma to cap the price of EpiPens at $60, passed restrictions on predatory debt collectors and payday lenders, and led the fight on common sense gun safety legislation. I also believe strongly in workers' rights more broadly. I was proud to be named the 2025 AFL-CIO Labor Champ, and expanding the rights of workers to organize and bargain collectively will always be central to my work. This work is personal. My mother was left permanently disabled after a near-fatal car crash and raised my brother and me on her Social Security Disability check alone. We had our power and water cut off. We relied on food banks. We were evicted and became homeless when I was fifteen. I got my GED, worked as a dishwasher and pizza delivery driver to put myself through community college, and took payday loans just to stay housed. That experience is why I became an eviction defense lawyer, why I helped found the Community Economic Defense Project, and why I have spent my career fighting for people the system has left behind. I believe the Democratic Party must return to its roots as an economically populist, working-class party. Working people are struggling not because of bad luck, but because of policy choices — and I am in this to change those choices.

My top priorities for this seat are: 1. Securing a site for a new homelessness navigator center; 2. Updating and beefing up oil and gas regulation; 3. Creating new data center regulations; 4. Raising the minimum wage; 5. Creating a "pollinator corridor." 

I am motivated to run for office because I am very concerned about the direction our community is going in. Corporations have too much power and ordinary people don't have enough power. 

I want my constituents to know that I value them and their perspectives, and will do my best to pass policies that represent their dreams and demands.

I always put people first. That's my priority and motivation. As an environmental nonprofit executive, I've dedicated my career to amplifying the voices of community members often left out of policy conversations. And as a longtime West Denver community member, I've organized my community to advocate for causes that center working families and our environment. As a mom, I know firsthand that our schools need more resources and that our teachers need more support. We need housing that people can actually afford, and childcare and healthcare that aren't driven by profits. Every issue comes back to putting people first. I'm ready to fight for working families, the communities we live in, and the future we deserve.
